detailedDerivation: Existence d(n)/n→c and reach give c≤2, R(x)=x/c+o(x), A(x)=(1−1/c)x+o(x), and uniform errors on bounded multiples. P98 is rederived by excluding victims dying before the first p-service row from its j distinct bookers; P99 adds reach-forbidden victims with p_i+s_i<p_j. Both exclusion classes lie below s_j and are disjoint from bookers.

With v_j=s_j/j, L=1+1/c, r_j=j/c+o(j) and m_i=i(1+bv_i)+o(i), the full union yields s_j≥j+r_j+#{i>r_j:m_i<j}. Weighted summation over j gives liminf(logJ)^−1Σ(v_i−L−φ(v_i))/i≥0. The sufficient j interval is (1+bv_i+ξ)i<j<i/(1/c+ξ); omitted proportional tails and integer boundaries have Oξ(1) weight.

For φ=[1/(1+bv)−1/c]+, H(v)=1/v+k(v−L−φ) is convex on[L,c] and[c,2]. Chord coefficient k equalizes outer endpoint values; the kink is smaller by(2−c)(k−1/(2c))≥0. Thus reciprocal-victim mean≤C, and actual victim census gives log-average Imm(h)/h≥V=1−C. V−1/(c+1)>0 because c²−c−1>0; V<1/2 because2c²−1>0.

MEX diagonal-rank counting bounds each live journal ceiling, giving cK_h≥B N−(c−1)h−Imm(h), while direct journal exclusions give K_h≥N/c−b h−Imm(h). Integrating the maximum at a fixed immortal host has exact coefficient Ψ=B²/[c(c−1+u)]+bz²/u. The line crossing is N=u h/z and is after birth/positivity thresholds. Summing hosts and Stieltjes integration gives the concave integrand g=uΨ, with bounded endpoint primitive.

The chord of g on[u0,1/2] at meanV yields U10. Independent polynomial expansion gives[-9,27,11,−58,25,22,−25,7]. Exact Bernstein positivity of its derivative on[9/5,15/8] and a90-step rational bracket prove the unique root c_*<1.868565865679.

The source’s vague prior upper-endpoint exclusion is replaced by a self-contained repair: the rank-integrated two-line MEX inequality M8 has positive surplus159327/60696000 at15/8. Its derivative is positive throughout[15/8,2), using |(1/(cD))′|<15/64 and positive derivative of(c−1)^3(c²−3)^2/(c³D). At c=2, a positive fraction of immortal hosts demandsΩ(N²) diagonal cells while row capacity is o(N²). Thus no c≥15/8 occurs; c<9/5 trivially satisfies the final bound.
